skills.name: automate-browser
skills.description: Automate a browser workflow — navigate, fill forms, click through flows, extract page data, take screenshots, or turn a repeated manual task into a reusable script — with the cheapest reliable browser tool available and explicit confirmation before anything outward-facing (submitting, purchasing, posting, sending). Use for "automate this browser workflow", "fill this form", "scrape this page", "click through this flow" or "make a script for this web task".

skills.name: build-animation
skills.description: Design and build motion that is calm, continuous and 60fps, respects reduced motion and pauses offscreen: hero animations, signature living visuals, transitions, scroll and micro-interactions, and WebGL, Canvas or SVG effects. Style add-ons (cinematic, claymorphism, glassmorphism) set the motion character on top of the shared calm feel. Includes cinematic-plate, which turns a reference image of a cinematic scene into a live web hero (a generated art plate plus thin live layers). Use for "add an animation", "hero animation", "make it move", a motion review, or replicating a cinematic reference.

skills.name: build-feature
skills.description: Build a feature end to end — ground it in the code, write a short brief, implement, test, verify on the real target and review. Scales from a small change (just do it and verify) to a large feature (spec first, worktree, parallel workers). Use when asked to build, add or implement a feature, "build this end to end", or "write a spec/brief" for one (the former /spec).

skills.name: coordinate-agents
skills.description: Split work across agents — delegate an isolated implementation to OpenAI Codex through codex-bridge in its own git worktree, run independent parts in parallel subagents, then review and integrate the results yourself. Includes the former /codex-frontend workflow. Use for "use Codex for this", "delegate to Codex", "split this work", "run agents in parallel" or "orchestrate agents".

skills.name: fix-bug
skills.description: Find and fix a bug — reproduce it on the real target, find the root cause, write a failing regression test, fix, and confirm the fix where the user saw the bug. Use for errors, crashes, failing tests or CI, wrong behavior, "this is broken", "still broken" or "I still see the old one".

skills.name: history-learning
skills.description: Learn durable preferences, corrections, decisions and working patterns from historical coding-agent conversations (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Antigravity, Kiro, Qwen) and turn them into reviewed, evidence-backed skill updates. Use when asked to learn from past conversations or chat history, mine repeated corrections or preferences, update skills from experience, run incremental history learning, or audit what has been learned. Read-only over history, consent-gated per source, redacts before any model sees text, and never publishes or overwrites skills on its own.

skills.name: improve
skills.description: Audit a project or area for improvements, rank them, implement the safe ones and verify them in one pass, then list the rest as numbered options. Also covers behavior-preserving refactors and measured performance work. Use when the user runs /improve [area], asks "what can be improved" (and would otherwise follow up with "implement all"), or asks to refactor, clean up or speed something up.

skills.name: manage-skills
skills.description: Manage this skill catalog — find which skill fits a request, create or update a skill, vet and adopt a third-party skill, reinstall or repair skill discovery for Claude, Codex and other agents, and learn new rules from past agent conversations (history-learning). Use for "which skill should I use", "add a skill", "update my skills", "install skills", "learn from my history" or when a skill seems missing or broken.

skills.name: night
skills.description: Run autonomous, verified improvement loops on a repository overnight or while away. It plans by priority, works on an isolated run branch, delegates each iteration to Claude, Codex or a configured agent, independently verifies and keeps or reverts every change, survives crashes through a watchdog, and writes an evidence-only morning report. Never pushes, merges or deploys. Use for "/night", "/night auto", "/night tests", "run loops overnight", "night status", "night report" or "stop the night run".

skills.name: night-accessibility
skills.description: Accessibility loop. Repair one evidenced interface barrier and retain it only when violation counts fall, keyboard paths work and no new barriers appear. Use for "night-accessibility", "night accessibility" or as /night accessibility.

skills.name: night-bug-hunter
skills.description: Bug-hunting loop. Start from a red baseline, reproduce one failure, add a failing regression test and repair its root cause, keeping the fix only when the original failure and relevant checks pass. Use for "night-bug-hunter", "night bug hunter" or as /night bugs.

skills.name: night-consistency
skills.description: Consistency loop. Select one naming, error-handling, component or theme-token inconsistency, align a bounded set with an established repository pattern, and retain it only when checks show no regression. Use for "night-consistency", "night consistency" or as /night consistency.

skills.name: night-dependencies
skills.description: Dependency loop. Review advisories and update one package or lockstep group with the project package manager, favour patch and minor releases, and keep only a tested change with a consistent lockfile. Use for "night-dependencies", "night dependencies" or as /night dependencies.

skills.name: night-docs
skills.description: Documentation loop. Find one mismatch between repository instructions and actual code, correct it with precise examples, and retain the edit only when the documented commands and claims are verified locally. Use for "night-docs", "night docs" or as /night docs.

skills.name: night-evolve-skills
skills.description: Skill-evolution loop. Improve one catalog skill from recorded failures and repeated corrections, validate the edit, and reserve changes to the active loop or engine for human application. Use for "night-evolve-skills", "night evolve skills" or as /night evolve-skills.

skills.name: night-ideas
skills.description: Idea loop. Rank product and engineering opportunities from repository evidence with explicit priority scores, returning actionable proposals and follow-ups without writing files. Use for "night-ideas", "night ideas" or as /night ideas.

skills.name: night-improve
skills.description: Improvement loop. Rank small repository improvements by evidence, make the best bounded change, and keep it only when checks prove the intended benefit without regressions. Use for "night-improve", "night improve" or as /night improve.

skills.name: night-performance
skills.description: Performance loop. Measure one real bottleneck with repeated baseline and candidate runs, make one bounded optimisation, and retain it only when the measured gain exceeds noise and behaviour stays stable. Use for "night-performance", "night performance" or as /night performance.

skills.name: night-qa
skills.description: User-flow QA loop. Exercise one main journey end to end, capture reproducible breaks, and add one regression-backed repair or a precise bug-hunter follow-up, with runtime evidence for every claim. Use for "night-qa", "night qa" or as /night qa.

skills.name: night-redteam
skills.description: Red-team loop. Prove one exploitable trust-boundary failure only with a local failing test, then repair its root cause or record an owner decision when no safe fix fits. Use for "night-redteam", "night redteam" or as /night redteam.

skills.name: night-refactor
skills.description: Refactoring loop. Characterise existing behaviour before simplifying one bounded area, preserve the public API, and keep the change only when tests and review show equivalent behaviour with less complexity. Use for "night-refactor", "night refactor" or as /night refactor.

skills.name: night-research
skills.description: Research loop. Investigate one repository question with primary sources and code evidence, then return a cited markdown report with confidence levels and unknowns, without changing any files in the worktree. Use for "night-research", "night research" or as /night research.

skills.name: night-tests
skills.description: Test-coverage loop. Each iteration finds the riskiest untested behavior, adds one focused test in the project's own style, proves it would catch a break, and keeps it only if the suite stays green. Use for "night-tests", "add tests overnight", "grow coverage in a loop" or as /night tests.

skills.name: night-visual
skills.description: Visual loop. Improve one evidenced interface issue, compare real screenshots in both themes and configured viewports, and retain the change only when visual review and runtime checks support it. Use for "night-visual", "night visual" or as /night visual.

skills.name: nightly-evolution
skills.description: Autonomous overnight improvement of a repository on an isolated nightly/evolution-YYYY-MM-DD branch, producing one evidence-backed draft PR per night. Covers performance, code quality, architecture, UI/UX, modernization, security, reliability, AI efficiency, cost, developer experience and product opportunities. Use on a night-loop tick, or when asked to "run nightly evolution", "evolve this repo overnight" or "do an improvement pass". Not for fixing a specific reported bug.

skills.name: production-ready
skills.description: Take a project from "works on my machine" to ready for real users: a readiness audit across security, tests, error handling and observability, performance, configuration and secrets, build and deploy, data safety and docs, then fix the gaps in priority order and prove each with evidence. Does not deploy or publish unless asked. Use for "make this project production ready", "prepare for launch", "harden this", "release readiness" or "is this ready to ship".

skills.name: research
skills.description: Research a topic, technology, library or question in depth: plan sub-questions, gather primary sources, cross-check claims, run a contrarian pass, and deliver a cited synthesis with confidence levels and what stays unknown. Also covers comparing libraries or tools, evaluating a repo before adopting it, and checking data or experiment results. Scales from a quick answer to a multi-agent deep dive. Use for "research this topic deeply", "compare X and Y", "evaluate this library" or "what's the state of the art".

skills.name: revamp-ui
skills.description: Revamp, redesign, polish or audit a UI (website, app, dashboard, landing page) to the owner's premium bar. It audits, picks a direction, fixes spacing, color, type, layout, details, visuals and motion, generates hero visuals when an image tool exists, and verifies with real screenshots in both themes. Scales from a quick polish to a full redesign with Codex concepts. Attaches a style add-on (cinematic, claymorphism, glassmorphism) on top of the general method. Includes unslop (remove AI-looking UI tells) and visual review against a reference. Use for "revamp my website UI", "make it look premium", "make it claymorphic/glassy/cinematic", "unslop", "redesign", "UI audit" or "match this reference".

skills.name: review-changes
skills.description: Show what a branch, PR or diff changes for a person, not as code. Interface changes appear as real before/after screenshots of the running app, side by side with a pixel diff, in both themes and at desktop and mobile widths. Backend changes become plain-English cards that say what changed, what it improves, the risk and how it could break, and a confidence level backed by evidence (a test that fails without the change, a run, or only a code read). Suggestions are cross-checked before they are shown. Use for "show me the changes", "before and after", "ui side by side", "visual diff of this branch", "change report" or "what did this PR change".

skills.name: review-code
skills.description: Review a diff, branch, commit or PR for real bugs, performance problems, needless complexity and missing tests, and verify every finding before reporting it. By default the review is an independent read-only pass by OpenAI Codex through codex-bridge (the former /codex-review); without the bridge it is a careful self-review. Use for "review this", "code review", "second opinion", "have Codex check it", or before calling a large change done.

skills.name: run-autonomous
skills.description: Run a long or multi-step task autonomously — overnight, while the user is away, or until a list of milestones is done — with an isolated branch or worktree, a written ledger of progress and decisions, bounded retries, and a final evidence-backed report. Includes the nightly-evolution routine (one draft PR of improvements per night). Never pushes, merges or deploys unless asked. Use for "run this task autonomously overnight", "keep going until done", "work on this while I sleep" or "run nightly evolution".

skills.name: security-audit
skills.description: Audit a codebase or change for security problems — secrets, authentication and authorization, injection, XSS/CSRF/SSRF, unsafe deserialization, dependency CVEs, risky install scripts, permissions and data exposure — with a threat model sized to the system, concrete exploit scenarios, and fixes. Also reviews third-party skills, plugins and MCP servers before adoption. Read-only unless fixes are asked for. Use for "security audit", "security review", "threat model", "is this safe" or "check for secrets".

skills.name: ship
skills.description: Ship finished work end to end once the user asks for it — run the checks, compare failures with a baseline on main, merge, push, deploy and health-check when the repo has a deploy step, then clean up this session's branches, worktrees and servers and report the commit. Use for "ship it", "merge and push", "merge, push and deploy", "merge to main and clean up" or "push everything and delete the branches". Not for deciding whether something is ready (production-ready) or for unasked releases.
aliases: merge to main and clean up

skills.name: test-everything
skills.description: Plan, write and run tests across the stack — unit, integration, end-to-end and visual — find the gaps that matter, fix flaky tests at the cause, and report real results. Use for "test everything", "add tests", "improve test coverage", "set up e2e tests", a test strategy, or when a change needs proof beyond reading the code.

skills.name: understand-code
skills.description: Understand and explain a codebase or one area of it — architecture, entry points, data flow, dependencies, conventions and risky spots — with file:line evidence, as a short map or a diagram. Use for "understand the architecture of this repository", "how does X work", "explain this codebase", onboarding, or before changing unfamiliar code.

skills.name: verify
skills.description: Verify a change where the user actually looks at it (local browser, Vercel/production URL, LG TV, Windows desktop app, Chrome extension) and report pass/fail with real evidence. Use when the user runs /verify, says something is "still broken" / "I still see the old one", or before claiming a UI or runtime fix is done.
aliases: i still see the old one

skills.name: working-agreements
skills.description: The owner's standing rules for any coding agent, learned from their own repeated instructions and corrections across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and Antigravity. Use at the start of any coding, debugging, UI or automation task in the owner's repositories; before reporting work as done or fixed; before any commit, push, merge, deploy or paid model call; when touching secrets, git state or another agent's work; during long autonomous or overnight runs; and for any UI, visual design or animation change. A repository's AGENTS.md and the current task's explicit instructions take precedence.
